summary: The one new item in the Fairbanks area on Monday, Nov. 9, is an arrest that Fairbanks Police added to their Nov. 8 bulletin overnight: Herbert Herbie Ipalook, 42, arrested on two misdemeanor assault counts at the 2000 block of Carr Avenue on Sunday lunchtime. No criminal case had been filed in court behind it as of Monday morning. No criminal case was opened at the Fairbanks, Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courthouses between Sunday afternoon and the morning of Nov. 9, and Alaska State Troopers had published no daily dispatch for Nov. 9 at that hour. The filing counts below are the Alaska Court System weekly charges report's own counts for its window of Nov. 2 to Nov. 8; that report was run at 9 p.m. on Nov. 8 and, unusually, includes both of the cases the Fairbanks court opened that afternoon. It also lists one Fairbanks case number, 4FA-26-02241CR, that the court's public database does not return, and a second case number opened on Nov. 8 has stopped being returned since. The statewide dispositions report has not been updated since Nov. 2, so no case closed in the Interior since then appears in any court document. The Fairbanks Daily News-Miner public safety column has published nothing since Nov. 6.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Herbert Herbie Ipalook
body: Herbert Herbie Ipalook, 42, was arrested on two counts, assault in the fourth degree and assault committed in the presence of a child. Assault in the fourth degree on this subsection means recklessly causing injury to another person. Fairbanks Police record both counts as misdemeanors.
According to Fairbanks Police, the arrest was made at the 2000 block of Carr Avenue in Fairbanks on Nov. 8 at 12:50 p.m. The case number is 26003402.

No criminal case had been filed in court behind the arrest as of the morning of Nov. 9. The Fairbanks criminal case series stands at 4FA-26-02254CR, and a statewide search of court records in this name returned no 2026 criminal case.

entries.title: Felony card-theft case set for a Nov. 10 hearing: Julia Ann Pitka
body: Julia Ann Pitka, 38, is charged with six counts arising from a Nov. 7 arrest in Fairbanks. Two are felony counts of theft in the second degree of an access device or identification document — taking someone else's credit card, debit card or identification — Class C felonies, punishable under Alaska law by up to five years. The other four are misdemeanors: fraudulent use of a stolen access device for less than $75, theft of property worth less than $250, and two counts of violating conditions of release in a felony case.
Fairbanks Police say the arrest was made at the 1100 block of Lakeview Terrace on Nov. 7 at 4:32 p.m. The counts carry offense dates of Nov. 6, the day before.
A status hearing is set for Nov. 10 at 1:30 p.m., with preliminary hearings on Nov. 18 and Nov. 25. Case 4FA-26-02250CR.

entries.title: Statewide court report on closed cases is a week out of date
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal cases disposed carries a footer stamp of Nov. 2 at 4 a.m. and covers cases closed between Oct. 1 and Nov. 2. It has not been refreshed since, through seven scheduled update cycles.

The practical effect is that no criminal case closed at the Fairbanks, Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courthouses since Nov. 2 — no conviction, acquittal, dismissal or sentence — appears in any published court document. Individual case files remain readable one at a time in the court's public database.
